title: A better covenant and a sacrifice once for all

passage.why: The author says it plainly: 'Now the point in what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest' (8:1). These chapters are the summit of Hebrews: the new covenant, the true sanctuary, and the one sacrifice that finishes the work.

readAloud: And every priest stands daily at his service, offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins. But when Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God, waiting from that time until his enemies should be made a footstool for his feet. For by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified. (Hebrews 10:11-14)
setting: The tabernacle Moses built was 'a copy and shadow of the heavenly things' (8:5). Once a year, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood (Leviticus 16). Hebrews reads that whole system as a picture of Christ, who entered heaven itself with his own blood.

sections.heading: The new covenant is here
sections.body: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah 31:31-34 in full (8:8-12), the longest Old Testament quotation in the New. 'I will put my laws into their minds, and write them on their hearts' (8:10). 'In speaking of a new covenant, he makes the first one obsolete' (8:13).

sections.heading: Once for all
sections.body: Christ 'entered once for all into the holy places... by means of his own blood, thus securing an eternal redemption' (9:12). His blood will 'purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God' (9:14). 'He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself' (9:26), and 'will appear a second time... to save those who are eagerly waiting for him' (9:28).

sections.heading: Shadow and substance
sections.body: 'The law has but a shadow of the good things to come' (10:1). 'It is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins' (10:4). Psalm 40 shows the Son coming to do God's will (10:5-7), and 'by that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all' (10:10).

sections.heading: He sat down, again
sections.body: The theme of session 1 returns: priests stand, Christ sat down (10:11-12). 'I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more' (10:17). 'Where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin' (10:18). The work is finished.

sections.heading: Perfected and being sanctified
sections.body: 'By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified' (10:14). Two tenses in one verse: a finished standing before God, and an ongoing growth in holiness. Traditions describe how the two relate differently, but all hold both.

observe: Mark every 'once' and 'once for all' in 9:1-10:18. What does the repetition say?
Compare what the old sacrifices could do (9:9-10; 10:1-4) with what Christ's sacrifice does (9:14; 10:10-14).
Which promises of Jeremiah 31 (8:10-12) do you most need to hear this week?

words.note: A go-between who guarantees an agreement between two parties (8:6; 9:15; 12:24).
Once, never to be repeated (7:27; 9:12; 10:10). The key word of these chapters.
The inner witness that accuses or excuses. The old sacrifices could not perfect it (9:9); Christ's blood cleanses it (9:14; 10:22).

crossRefs.note: 'I have come to do your will'.
The new covenant in my blood.
No condemnation, in your reading spine.

reflect: What 'dead works' (9:14) is my conscience still trying to pay for?
How does 'I will remember their sins no more' sit with how I remember my own?
Where do I live as if the work were not finished?

practice.name: Finished, so serve
practice.how: Write down one thing you keep re-confessing or re-paying in your mind. Read 10:17-18 over it, then tear the paper up. Choose one act of service this week that comes from gratitude, not guilt (9:14).

pray: Adoration: a high priest seated at the right hand. Confession: dead works I still lean on. Thanksgiving: sins remembered no more. Supplication: a clean conscience to serve the living God at home and at Eden.
journalPrompts: What did I learn about God this week, from the reading or from life?
Where did I see Jesus as better this week than the thing I was leaning on?
What question did this passage raise that I want to bring to my pastor or Micah?
